The treated amblyopia (lazy eye) in children did not significantly change choroidal thickness. Our results showed that six months of treatment with a specific dosage of the medication resulted in an improvement in visual acuity in the affected eye, but had no effect on choroidal thickness. This suggests that subfoveal choroidal thickness in amblyopic children may not be responsive to treatment.

In other words, while the treatment of amblyopia did improve the visual function of the affected eye and increased its visual acuity, it did not lead to a change in the underlying structure of the retina or choroid in these children. This means that the subfoveal choroidal thickness remains unaffected by this treatment approach.
